name: High quality microbial and fungal community in Soil
problem_statement: Farmers across a range of scales (from private gardens to large farms) need better understanding, engineering, and injection of soil microbial and fungal communities in order to improve soil quality, crop production, and resilience to extreme weather events such as heat and flooding.
objective: Identify research on microbial and fungal community management strategies that enhance soil health, crop productivity, and resistance to extreme heat and flooding stress.

technology_focus: Stress tolerance in crops and soils

must_have: Paper addresses microbial or fungal communities in agricultural soils
Paper relates to at least one of: soil quality, crop production, crop/soil health, or stress resistance
nice_to_have: Covers both small-scale and large-scale farming contexts
exclusions: Studies focused solely on non-agricultural soils (e.g. mining, industrial sites) with no relevance to crop systems

notes: Scope covers the full range of farm sizes, from individual gardens to large commercial farms. Both microbial and fungal communities are of interest. Key outcomes of interest are soil quality, crop yield, and resilience to extreme heat and flooding.
